messages:
maria-ng: Heads-up — saw a nasty case in last night's canary. Tenant hit quota cap, routing policy auto-fell back to a tiny quantized variant and the outputs degraded (hallucinations). We should not silently pick the smallest variant when quota is the cause.

nishant: Oof. Do we have logs/traces? curious whether the decision engine labeled it 'capacity' vs 'quota'.

maria-ng: Logs attached to the incident but tl;dr: decision path = capacity_check -> fail -> pick lowest-cost compatible variant -> success. No special handling for tenant quota. ops-bot also fired an alert.

ops-bot: Alert: quota breach for tenant=acme-corp, region=us-west-2, rate=1.9x quota, timestamp=2123456700

kevin_p: Two quick thoughts: (1) fallback reason should be explicit (quota vs node preempt) and surfaceable in the UI + telemetry. (2) For quota-origin fallbacks, prefer a graceful degrade (truncate prompt / reduce max_tokens) before swapping model variant.

console-team: +1 on surfacing reason. From a UX perspective we can show a "fallback reason" pill in the rollout timeline and annotate canary samples that were affected. Also suggest adding a short human-readable rationale in the rollout detail so PMs can triage.

eva_prod: Telemetry ask: capture pre/post quality metrics for any fallback during experiments (per-tenant). Names: fallback_reason, fallback_variant, fallback_quality_delta, affected_sample_count. We need to ensure A/B tooling doesn't mix these samples into the control bucket.

nishant: Agreed. Also let's add a small budget-check step in the runtime decision graph. Proposal (pseudocode):
```
# runtime fallback heuristic (simplified)
if tenant.quota.remaining < min_tokens_needed:
  mark_reason = 'quota'
  if tenant.flags.allow_truncate:
    reduce max_tokens by 30%
  else:
    route_to('graceful-lite-variant')
else:
  normal_capacity_flow()
```
This keeps the variant swap as a last resort.

maria-ng: I like keeping variant swap last resort. We also need a console knob to set per-tenant fallback policy (force-truncate / allow-variant-swap / hold-traffic). Must be editable without deploy.

kevin_p: And we should clamp canary weights when quota-limited tenants are in the sample set. e.g., auto-detect high-risk tenants and reduce their canary exposure to 0% to avoid noisy spikes breaking the experiment.

console-team: Implementation note: we can add a 'risk-exclude' tag on tenant rows, and a quick filter in the rollout create flow: "exclude quota-constrained tenants". Small UI change, low-risk.

eva_prod: For evals, surface a small heatmap that shows where fallbacks concentrated (tenant, region, model-variant). This will make post-mortems faster.

nishant: I'll open an RFC that bundles: 1) runtime budget-aware decision step, 2) telemetry fields (as listed by @eva_prod), 3) console UX (fallback reason pill + tenant-exclude), 4) runbook updates for oncall. Will include a sample rollout policy YAML.

maria-ng: Sample YAML suggestion — include tenant_quota_policy and fallback_priority: 
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  tenant_quota_policy:
    truncate_before_variant: true
    min_remaining_tokens: 100
  fallback_priority:
    - graceful_truncate
    - degrade_variant: graceful-lite-8bit
    - regional_failover
```

deploy-bot: deploy.git: canary-routing v2 pushed by nishant at 2123456745 — will be on staging in 10m.

kevin_p: One more: add an explainability tag that returns the short decision trace for each request (very small token cost). Console can show it for samples. Helps PMs and SREs debug.

nishant: Good call. I'll add `decision_trace_id` into telemetry and an endpoint to fetch the trace.

maria-ng: Action items: @nishant open RFC + PR for runtime; @console-team prototype pill + exclusion filter; @eva_prod add telemetry dashboard mock; ops watch for repeat quota breaches and we may need a global quota-slowdown policy.

console-team: We can mock the pill in the staging console tomorrow.

nishant: RFC created: https://rbx.internal/rfcs/9876 (WIP) — PR will reference it. I'll also create a Jira: PLAT-4521 (runtime), PLAT-4522 (console), PLAT-4523 (telemetry).

maria-ng: Great. Thanks all. If we can land a staging rollout with the clamp and the pill visible, we can test with a few known quota tenants tomorrow. :thumbsup:
